title: Stop abuse of seasonal and tourist lets
detail: End fraudulent "seasonal" contracts (*alquiler de temporada*) used to dodge the protections of a main-home lease, and regulate seasonal and tourist lets so they do not take homes off the market. The programme contains no rent cap.
c: Closing the seasonal-let loophole is a simple change to the LAU, with broad support.
pos: Closes the loophole used to get around tenant protections.
neg: Harder for students and posted workers to find temporary housing.

title: Zero or super-reduced VAT on basic food
detail: A broad VAT reform with zero or super-reduced rates (*IVA superreducido*) on some basic foods (fish, meat and others) and specific products (for coeliacs and others), plus a review of taxes on electricity, gas, fuel and public transport within EU rules.
c: 0% on basic food already applied in 2023–24, and the EU directive allows it. The cut reached prices almost in full (Banco de España, CNMC); the Fedea think tank estimated that half the savings went to the best-off 40% of households.
pos: Cheaper food, especially for poorer households.
neg: Half the savings went to the best-off 40% of households in 2023, according to Fedea; lost revenue.

s.t: Banco de España, Working Paper 2417 (2024): VAT cut pass-through to prices
CNMC, 10 Aug 2023: study of the VAT cut pass-through to food prices
Fedea (think tank), López Laborda et al., Apuntes 2023/02: who gained from the VAT cut

title: Cut the electricity tax to 0.5%
detail: Permanently cut the special electricity tax (*Impuesto Especial sobre la Electricidad*) to 0.5%, within EU limits.
c: The EU minimum is €0.5/MWh for business and €1/MWh for households; a 0.5% rate already applied in 2021–23. Realistic; in our estimate it costs about €1.5 billion a year.
pos: Cheaper electricity and an incentive to electrify.
neg: Lost revenue that goes to the regions.

s.t: Directive 2003/96/EC on energy taxation: minimum €0.5/€1 per MWh (BOE copy of the OJEU)

title: Index pensions to inflation; raise minimum pensions gradually
detail: Index pensions to consumer prices (*IPC*) every year, and raise minimum and non-contributory pensions (*pensión no contributiva*) "gradually", focusing on the lowest incomes. No amounts.
c: Indexation to the CPI is already in law.
neg: Spending rises as the population ages.

title: No early-retirement penalty after 40 years of contributions
detail: Remove early-retirement penalties (*coeficiente reductor*) for people with more than 40 years of contributions, with measures to correct the penalties for people already retired.
c: Realistic; applying it to people already retired costs more. It matches Junts and Podemos, so a majority is possible.
pos: Fairness for people who have worked 40 years or more.
neg: Higher spending, and it runs against the aim of longer working lives.

title: A Basque minimum wage above the national one
detail: As part of a new political status, seek full power to set a Basque minimum wage (*SMI*) adapted to living costs and always above the national minimum, agreed through social dialogue (*diálogo social*). No amount.
c: A separate minimum wage needs power over labour law (art. 149.1.7 of the Constitution); the "new political status" itself would require reforms.

title: Defend and widen the Basque *Concierto Económico*
detail: Amend the *Concierto Económico* law to widen Basque financial and tax powers, and make sure state tax and budget reforms respect it; defend Navarre's *Convenio Económico* as well.
c: The *concierto* law is changed by agreement in a joint commission; widening it is realistic under a government that depends on PNV.
pos: More tax powers for the Basque Country.
neg: Deepens the conflict with other regions over solidarity.
